sources.title: Getty ULAN: Bhupatindra Malla
sources.note: Getty authority record identifying Bhupatindra as Bhaktapur ruler from 1696 to 1722 and continuing architectural patronage.

sources.title: Kathmandu Valley World Heritage property
sources.note: UNESCO synthesis of the three urban centers, religious coexistence, craft media, urban fabric, and 1500 to 1800 artistic flowering.

sources.title: Kathmandu Valley advisory body evaluation
sources.note: Institutional assessment of rival Malla kingdoms, monuments, urban ensembles, crafts, rebuilding, and preservation limits.

sources.title: Language of Prithvimalla and Pratap Malla inscriptions
sources.note: University philology article dating the Rani Pokhari text to 1670 and analyzing Sanskrit, Middle Nepali, and Newari passages.

sources.title: The Rani Pokhri Inscription, Kathmandu
sources.note: SOAS study based on rubbings and photographs of the multilingual inscription, pond, temple, canal, sacred waters, and uncertain readings.

sources.title: Nepali: The Emergence of a National Language

sources.title: Tantra in Practice: royal Taleju text
sources.note: Scholarly edition contextualizing Pratap Malla's mid-seventeenth-century Sanskrit praise poem and Taleju royal ritual.

sources.title: Theatre of Nepal excerpt
sources.note: Cambridge history of Malla court and public performance, dabali stages, audiences, patronage, and later memory.

sources.title: Katti Pyakha: A Case Study
sources.note: Tribhuvan University study of a Patan dance tradition linked to Siddhinarasimha and Srinivasa, with transmission cautions.

sources.title: Gorkha Durbar Care Office history
sources.note: Official heritage history describing Baisi and Chaubisi states, Gorkha, Lamjung rivalry, agriculture, forts, and source uncertainty.

sources.title: Nepal and Bhutan country studies
sources.note: Library of Congress study separating the three Valley kingdoms, Chaubisi near west, Baisi far west, and Jumla leadership.

sources.title: Caste and Kinship in a Newar Village
sources.note: Oxford Academic chapter on caste, guthi organization, patrilineal kinship, joint families, religion, residence, and the limits of generalization.

sources.title: Contested Hierarchies
sources.note: Oxford Academic book overview identifying priests, patrons, artisans, farmers, merchants, and low castes while emphasizing variation within a regional system.

sources.title: Buddhist Merchants in Kathmandu
sources.note: Oxford ethnography and ethnohistory of the Asan market, Uray merchants, caste institutions, and Kathmandu as a Malla polity.

sources.title: Man, religion and agriculture in the Kathmandu Valley
sources.note: Academic study of small farms, multiple occupations, caste-linked labor, pottery seasons, tenancy, and later continuities.

sources.title: Street typology in Kathmandu and street transformation
sources.note: Academic urban study of Malla-period courtyards, multistory houses, lanes, squares, monasteries, and caste-marked spatial hierarchy.

sources.title: Economic and Social Conditions of Medieval Nepal
sources.note: Scholarly review of agriculture, trade, artisans, markets, festivals, labor, and gaps in medieval economic evidence.

sources.title: Caste System in Medieval Nepal
sources.note: Tribhuvan University Journal study of medieval occupational ranking, discriminatory rules, residence, dress, and later claims about Jayasthiti Malla.

sources.title: From Royal Canal to Neglected Canal?
sources.note: Springer academic chapter on Kathmandu Valley rajkulo canals, irrigated farming, ponds, settlement supply, royal sanction, guthi support, and changing management.

sources.title: Understanding the Local Context for Sustainable Water Management
sources.note: Institutional case study of Bhaktapur rajkulo supply, spout drainage, wastewater flow, rituals, and guthi maintenance.

sources.title: Traditional wastewater management in Nepal
sources.note: University repository report documenting later Newar sinks, clay drains, compost pits, and reuse while leaving early dates uncertain.

sources.title: Interpreting the Ayurvedic Man
sources.note: Museum research on an eighteenth-century Nepalese medical manuscript, Bhavaprakasha, physicians, Tibetan artists, and Kathmandu collaboration.

sources.title: The Licchavi Susrutasamhita
sources.note: Scholarly history-of-medicine presentation on an older Nepalese medical manuscript, scribes, physicians, textual transmission, and access limits.

sources.title: The Development of Vihara Culture
sources.note: Scholarly study of Valley viharas as religious, residential, educational, manuscript, and cultural institutions.

sources.title: Social consequences of marrying Visnu Narayana
sources.note: Peer-reviewed modern ethnography of Newar life-cycle ritual, marriage, gender, and variation, used only as later evidence.

sources.title: Documents on the System of Sati
sources.note: Heidelberg Academy research project treating sati through pre-modern Nepalese documents and legal-religious contexts.

sources.title: Sati Custom in Nepal: A Historical Perspective
sources.note: Academic article assembling inscriptional examples, including elite and non-elite cases in the late seventeenth century.

sources.title: The Institution of Slavery in Nepal and its Analysis Based on the Dharmasastras
sources.note: Scholarly legal-historical chapter on slavery in Nepal, Malla documents, law, purchase, dependency, and interpretive limits.

sources.title: Durga and the Kings of Nepal
sources.note: Heidelberg research on Mahanī, distinct Malla royal ritual practices, Tantric liturgy, specialists, and later state transformation.

sources.title: Divinized protection: inscribed shields from Malla Nepal
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study of inscribed ritual objects, Sanskrit and Newari manuscripts, goddess systems, kingship, and dating.

sources.title: Changu Narayan Temple
sources.note: Nepal Tourism Board institutional description of the temple, inscriptions, sectarian overlap, and religious landscape.

sources.title: Ancient Nepal journal: terracotta art tradition

proposedOverrides.summary: Atlas-audited guide to the divided Malla Valley and western Himalayan states from 1650 to 1700.

batchIdentityNotes: The exact nepal-1650 Polygon is a coarse atlas aggregate. It excludes Kathmandu, Patan, Bhaktapur, Kirtipur, and Banepa while including six tested western or central points.
Seventeenth-century Kathmandu, Patan, and Bhaktapur were rival Malla kingdoms. Western Baisi and Chaubisi states, including Gorkha and Jumla, were politically distinct.
The target is separate from nepal, nepal-1492, and nepal-1783. Shared display names do not authorize shared cards or geometries.
The Mughal Empire replacement at 1700 is a false political ending. It records an atlas seam, not conquest or social disappearance.
Court, temple, inscriptional, museum, and later ethnographic sources preserve unequal viewpoints and are not projected across all residents.
Sati, slavery, compulsory labor, caste exclusion, blockade, and war are treated as human costs and never romanticized.
